dek: See why tenant filtering must happen before similarity ranking: once a foreign chunk wins retrieval, asking the model to forget it is already too late.
story_heading: The most similar answer belongs to someone else
story: You are reviewing a retrieval assistant shared by multiple bank tenants. A semantic query can find a highly similar foreign policy before the system checks who is allowed to see it. Follow the candidate set from the active tenant boundary into model context.
goal: Use one wire-policy search to prove that tenant authorization must constrain retrieval candidates before similarity ranking, not after the model has seen them.
tip: Compare the candidate set before ranking, the selected document's tenant, and the provenance check. Each tenant has multiple policy documents, so similarity is useful for ranking within an eligible set; it is never an authorization decision.
reader_question: Can semantic similarity retrieve a more relevant policy from a tenant the signed-in user cannot access?
success_check: You can show that Hardened removes foreign documents from the candidate set before similarity ranking and model context.
technical_intro: This is a retrieval authorization test. Tenant eligibility must constrain the candidate set before semantic ranking; filtering after retrieval cannot undo a cross-tenant disclosure to the model.
reader_do: Compare the global candidate set with the tenant-prefiltered set, then inspect the selected document's tenant and provenance before reading the answer.
architecture_intro: The signed-in tenant supplies an authorization scope to retrieval. The critical ordering is ACL eligibility first, semantic ranking second, and provenance validation again before model context.
walkthrough_intro: Run the global-scope wire-policy request and use Compare 3 modes. Inspect eligible candidates before ranking, selected tenant and similarity metadata, then the provenance and output-DLP decisions.

vulnerable.authority: Global retriever scope and similarity ranking
vulnerable.scope: All policy documents in the shared corpus
vulnerable.mechanism: The retriever ranks Acme and Northstar candidates together and places the most similar foreign chunk in model context

prompt_only.authority: Model instruction to stay within Acme Bank
prompt_only.scope: Still the globally ranked shared corpus
prompt_only.enforcement: A model judgment after the retriever has selected evidence
prompt_only.mechanism: A migration pretext can relax the guard while the retriever continues to rank foreign candidates
prompt_only.proof: The foreign candidate remains eligible before the model is asked to ignore it

hardened.authority: Active-tenant ACL and bounded document_read tool
hardened.scope: Documents whose tenant equals the authenticated Acme Bank tenant
hardened.enforcement: Before semantic ranking, with provenance checked again after retrieval
hardened.mechanism: The database query pre-filters eligible tenants; the wrapper rejects out-of-scope tenant IDs and rechecks returned provenance

threat_model: Multiple bank tenants share a retrieval corpus. A semantically strong query can rank a foreign policy above the caller's own document. Tenant eligibility is therefore a database concern that must constrain the candidate set before query-dependent ranking.
attack_path: The user asks the agent to compare every tenant's wire-transfer policy.
Groq creates a semantic query and requests global scope.
The unsafe retriever ranks the shared corpus without first enforcing the active tenant ACL.
A more similar foreign document and its contact data enter model context and are returned.
prompt_only_failure: A model guard can be told to stay within Acme Bank, but the retriever-not the guard-selects evidence. A migration pretext can pass the model judgment, leaving the globally ranked tool to cross the tenant boundary.

hardened_controls.name: Admission gate
hardened_controls.detail: Hardened mode rejects obvious unrelated or override/bulk-access messages before retrieval planning; policy questions still demonstrate tenant pre-filtering.

hardened_controls.name: Pre-filter tenant ACL
hardened_controls.detail: Database policy restricts eligible documents to acme-bank before the semantic query is ranked.

hardened_controls.name: Bound tool scope
hardened_controls.detail: The document_read wrapper rejects a tenant ID outside the application-bound tenant.

hardened_controls.name: Fail-closed provenance
hardened_controls.detail: Every returned record is checked again for authorized tenant provenance before model context.

hardened_controls.name: Independent output DLP
hardened_controls.detail: Candidate output is checked for foreign provenance and unauthorized contact data without reading denied documents.

observe: Compare global-ranking and tenant-prefilter query descriptions in the trace.
Inspect the selected document's tenant, source, and similarity metadata.
Confirm that hardened evidence contains zero cross-tenant candidates even for a global-scope request.
engineering_notes: The miniature corpus has multiple documents per tenant and uses deterministic stored similarity values so both isolation and ranking remain reproducible.
Authorization changes candidate eligibility; it does not ask the model to post-filter a foreign result.
Provenance is preserved alongside content so later controls can verify origin explicitly.
